domain: Constitutional Law / Political Theory / Rights Jurisprudence
topic_summary: Analysis of the Second Amendment as a contested kernel where identical constitutional text ('A well regulated Militia, being necessary to the security of a free State, the right of the people to keep and bear Arms, shall not be infringed') is read as either an individual right to firearms ownership or a collective right tied to militia service. Each reading instantiates a structurally different constraint with distinct beneficiary/victim sets and enforcement mechanisms.

key_entities: Second Amendment text (constitutional kernel: 27 words, ratified 1791)
Supreme Court (interpretive authority post-Marbury; final arbiter of constitutional meaning)
Individual rights advocates (NRA, gun rights organizations, originalist scholars)
Collective rights advocates (gun control organizations, living constitutionalists)
State militias / National Guard (institutional embodiment of 'well regulated Militia')
Federal/state legislatures (regulatory authority constrained by judicial interpretation)
key_tensions: Prefatory clause ('well regulated Militia') vs operative clause ('right of the people') — grammatical structure contested as limiting or explanatory
Originalist textualism vs living constitutionalism — interpretive methodology determines which historical context controls
key_mechanisms: Judicial review (Supreme Court opinions establish binding precedent; Heller 2008 and McDonald 2010 instantiated individual-right reading)
Stare decisis (precedent stability vs overruling; individual-right reading now embedded but contested)
Legislative constraint (gun regulations must survive strict/intermediate scrutiny under current doctrine)
key_absences: Absence of explicit individual/collective distinction in text itself — ambiguity is structural feature, not drafting error
Absence of militia-service requirement in post-Heller doctrine — prefatory clause treated as non-operative

readings.authority_grounding: Civic republican synthesis (middle position: individual right exists but tied to collective defense function)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Militia-eligible individuals in beneficiary set; regulatory authority moderate; moderate ε with service-based gating

omegas.description: Does the prefatory clause ('well regulated Militia') limit the operative clause or merely explain one purpose? Grammatical structure contested; no consensus among linguists or historians. Individual reading treats as explanatory; collective reading treats as limiting. Civic reading treats as conditional.

Does 'the people' in Second Amendment refer to individuals (as in First/Fourth Amendments) or collective body politic? Individual reading: individuals. Collective reading: people-as-state. Civic reading: people-as-militia-eligible-citizens. Same term, three referents.
omegas.source: Kernel ambiguity (term appears in multiple amendments with potentially different meanings)

omegas.description: Is Heller (2008) stable precedent or vulnerable to overruling? Stare decisis doctrine suggests stability, but 5-4 decision and ongoing political contestation create uncertainty. If overruled, collective reading could return as dominant doctrine.

Are state militias (now National Guard) structurally obsolete for constitutional interpretation? If militia clause is non-operative (Heller position), does this render collective reading historically moot? Or does obsolescence itself argue for living constitutionalism?
omegas.source: Absence inventory: militia-service requirement absent in post-Heller doctrine

omegas.description: Post-Heller cases apply varying levels of scrutiny (strict, intermediate, rational basis) to gun regulations. No consensus on standard. This uncertainty affects ε measurement for individual reading — constraint may be weaker in practice than doctrine suggests.
omegas.source: Primary observable uncertainty: level of scrutiny applied to regulations

omegas.description: Civic right reading has no current Supreme Court support but represents coherent structural position. Could emerge if Court seeks middle ground or if militia service becomes politically salient. Currently speculative but structurally valid.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan): civic reading benefits neither current coalition

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel structure confirmed: three readings emit genuinely different constraints (different beneficiary sets, different ε values, different regulatory authority scope) from identical 27-word text. Readings are structurally independent (not merely different opinions about same constraint). Deferred axes are methodological mountains and meta-constraints, not alternative readings of the kernel itself.
